correctness.rationale: In a finite chain factor of length \(\ell\), annihilator classes are exactly the valuation levels \(0,\ldots,\ell\). For a product, vertices are all valuation vectors except the unit and zero vectors, and adjacency is the coordinatewise condition \(a_i+b_i\ge\ell_i\). Hence \(T=|V|+2=\prod_i(\ell_i+1)\) and \(d(a)=\prod_i(a_i+1)-1-\delta(a)\), with the self-exclusion term exactly when \(2a_i\ge\ell_i\) for all coordinates. When there are at least two factors, the leaves are exactly the coordinate vectors \(e_i\). Their unique neighbors have degrees \(T/2-1\) for \(\ell_i=1\) and \(T\ell_i/(\ell_i+1)-2\) for \(\ell_i\ge2\), recovering every length. The only numerical overlap is harmless at \(T=6\) and exceptional at \(T=4\), where \(\{3\}\) and \(\{1,1\}\) both give \(K_2\). One-factor cases are separated by order and leaf count. Fresh direct graph reconstruction reproduced the exceptional collision and representative mixed-length degree profiles; the bundled verifier stress-tests 225 additional length multisets.

originality.rationale: Alvir proves that matching irreducible-exponent patterns are sufficient for compressed-graph isomorphism for principal quotients of UFDs, explicitly observes the unlooped collision between a cube prime-power quotient and a product of two distinct prime quotients, and proves necessity only in the pure-prime-power and square-free subfamilies. The audited theorem extends this to all finite commutative principal ideal rings and proves that the displayed \(K_2\) collision is the only failure of chain-length recovery. Anderson--LaGrange study structural properties of the compressed graph but the accessible scope does not state this classification. Current Resultary search returned the assigned theorem as the exact hit and no stronger prior reconstruction theorem.
residual_risks: The Anderson--LaGrange full publisher manuscript was not available through the inspected public route, leaving a residual risk of an unadvertised isomorphism result.

value.rationale: Recovering ring structure from compressed zero-divisor graphs is the motivating question of the literature. The theorem gives a complete reconstruction invariant for all finite commutative principal ideal rings and proves that a previously known collision is uniquely exceptional. This is a natural classification theorem, not a recomputation of a few graph tables.
